title: Mobile: ReflectionProbe reflections are twice as bright as in Forward+, and clip at radiance 1.0
body:
### Tested versions

- Reproducible in: v4.7.2.stable.official [ed1daf0bf], v4.6.2.stable.official [71f334935]
- Not tested on 4.5. Reading the 4.5-stable source, probes were written and read with the same multiplier there (see below), so this may be a regression from #109971 (4.6).
- Not tested on `master`. The code involved is unchanged as of 12c17c187.

### System information

Godot v4.7.2.stable - macOS Tahoe (26.6.2) - Metal 4.0 (Mobile) - integrated Apple M5 Max (Apple9) - Apple M5 Max (18 threads) - 128.00 GiB memory

### Issue description

On the Mobile renderer, a ReflectionProbe returns about twice the radiance it captured. Because of this, anything brighter than 1.0 in the probe is clipped to 1.0 before it is doubled.

Test scene: a mirror sphere (metallic 1, roughness 0) at the centre of a ReflectionProbe (Update Mode: Once). It is surrounded by unshaded panels of known linear radiance under a uniform sky of 0.6. The value is read at the centre of the sphere, which reflects the panel behind the camera, and is divided by the tonemap exposure (linear tonemapper). HDR 2D is off except in the last column:

| Reflected source | Seen directly | Forward+ mirror | Mobile mirror | Mobile mirror, HDR 2D on |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| panel 0.25 | 0.252 | 0.252 | 0.499 | 0.495 |
| panel 0.50 | 0.499 | 0.499 | 0.985 | 0.990 |
| panel 0.90 | 0.893 | 0.893 | 1.781 | 1.780 |
| panel 1.60 | 1.608 | 1.608 | 1.988 | 1.978 |
| panel 1.90 | 1.894 | 1.894 | 1.988 | 1.978 |
| sky 0.60 (captured by the probe) | 0.600 | 0.600 | 1.185 | 1.187 |
| sky 0.60, mirror outside any probe | 0.600 | 0.600 | 0.588 | 0.593 |

- Below 1.0, Mobile reflects 1.97 to 1.99 times the source. Forward+ reflects 1.00 times.
- The 1.6 and 1.9 panels come back with the same value (1.988, or 1.978 with HDR 2D), so the probe holds 1.0 for both and the shader doubles it. The Mobile renderer's documented range is up to 2.0 ([`Environment.glow_hdr_threshold`](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/ed1daf0bf001b61586d9930840f2f1394092c079/doc/classes/Environment.xml#L148)), so the probe should be able to hold values up to 2.0.
- Sky reflections outside the probe are correct on Mobile (0.59 for 0.60), so only the probe path is affected.
- Enabling HDR 2D (here `SubViewport.use_hdr_2d`), which was suggested in https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/123733#issuecomment-5800246583, does not change the result.


**What the source seems to show (4.7.2-stable):**

- Mobile reads the probe atlas multiplied by `REFLECTION_MULTIPLIER`, which is a fixed `2.0` ("only for sky and reflection probes since they are always LDR"): [scene_forward_mobile_inc.glsl#L238-L240](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/ed1daf0bf001b61586d9930840f2f1394092c079/servers/rendering/renderer_rd/shaders/forward_mobile/scene_forward_mobile_inc.glsl#L238-L240) and [scene_forward_lights_inc.glsl#L1359](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/ed1daf0bf001b61586d9930840f2f1394092c079/servers/rendering/renderer_rd/shaders/scene_forward_lights_inc.glsl#L1359) (L1391 for clearcoat). The atlas uses Mobile's `DATA_FORMAT_A2B10G10R10_UNORM_PACK32` ([light_storage.cpp#L2048-L2050](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/ed1daf0bf001b61586d9930840f2f1394092c079/servers/rendering/renderer_rd/storage_rd/light_storage.cpp#L2048-L2050), [render_forward_mobile.cpp#L459-L462](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/ed1daf0bf001b61586d9930840f2f1394092c079/servers/rendering/renderer_rd/forward_mobile/render_forward_mobile.cpp#L459-L462)).
- The probe faces are rendered with the atlas's own render buffers ([renderer_scene_cull.cpp#L3821](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/ed1daf0bf001b61586d9930840f2f1394092c079/servers/rendering/renderer_scene_cull.cpp#L3821)). Those buffers are created with `instantiate()` ([light_storage.cpp#L1710-L1712](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/ed1daf0bf001b61586d9930840f2f1394092c079/servers/rendering/renderer_rd/storage_rd/light_storage.cpp#L1710-L1712)) and not through `render_buffers_create()`, which calls `set_can_be_storage(_render_buffers_can_be_storage())`, i.e. `false` on Mobile ([renderer_scene_render_rd.cpp#L241-L245](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/ed1daf0bf001b61586d9930840f2f1394092c079/servers/rendering/renderer_rd/renderer_scene_render_rd.cpp#L241-L245)). So `can_be_storage` keeps its default of `true` ([render_scene_buffers_rd.h#L70](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/ed1daf0bf001b61586d9930840f2f1394092c079/servers/rendering/renderer_rd/storage_rd/render_scene_buffers_rd.h#L70)), and `get_luminance_multiplier()` returns `1.0` for probe renders ([render_scene_buffers_rd.cpp#L861-L865](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/ed1daf0bf001b61586d9930840f2f1394092c079/servers/rendering/renderer_rd/storage_rd/render_scene_buffers_rd.cpp#L861-L865)).
- The probe pass then writes radiance multiplied by 1. This covers the scene shader output ([render_forward_mobile.cpp#L1182](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/ed1daf0bf001b61586d9930840f2f1394092c079/servers/rendering/renderer_rd/forward_mobile/render_forward_mobile.cpp#L1182) and [scene_forward_mobile.glsl#L2355-L2356](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/ed1daf0bf001b61586d9930840f2f1394092c079/servers/rendering/renderer_rd/shaders/forward_mobile/scene_forward_mobile.glsl#L2355-L2356)) and the sky and clear colour ([render_forward_mobile.cpp#L1062](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/ed1daf0bf001b61586d9930840f2f1394092c079/servers/rendering/renderer_rd/forward_mobile/render_forward_mobile.cpp#L1062)). The reader multiplies by 2, and the UNORM atlas clips at 1.0.
- In 4.5-stable, both sides used `_render_buffers_get_luminance_multiplier()`, which always returned `2.0` on Mobile ([4.5-stable render_forward_mobile.cpp#L419-L423](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/4.5-stable/servers/rendering/renderer_rd/forward_mobile/render_forward_mobile.cpp#L419-L423); the probe read was `* sc_luminance_multiplier()`). #109971 made the multiplier depend on the render buffers and added `REFLECTION_MULTIPLIER`. #113597 was another side effect of that change.

Related: the author of #123733 noted that Mobile reflections "seem to be way overly bright". #117833 is a different issue (rough metals reflecting the sky slightly darker because of the single-scattering BRDF; it does not involve probes).

The script also prints a clearcoat line, which is a separate issue and can be ignored here. Setting the probe's `intensity` to 0.5 on Mobile compensates for the doubling below 1.0, but not for the clipping.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Create a new project and a scene with a `Node3D` root. Attach the script below and set the scene as the main scene.
2. Run with `--rendering-method mobile`, then with `--rendering-method forward_plus` (or change the renderer in the Project Settings).
3. Compare the printed `probe, ...` lines. Mobile prints a ratio of about 1.98 for sources below 1.0, and the same reflected value (1.988) for the 1.6 and 1.9 panels. Forward+ prints `ratio 1.00` throughout.

### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)

No other files are needed besides the script (no imported assets):

```gdscript
extends Node3D
# Attach to the root Node3D of an empty scene and run it, once with the Mobile renderer and
# once with Forward+ (e.g. --rendering-method mobile / forward_plus). Prints measured radiance.

const SKY := 0.6  # radiance of a uniform sky
const PANELS := {  # unshaded panels 9 m from the probe centre: direction -> radiance
	Vector3(0, 0, -1): 0.25,
	Vector3(0, 0, 1): 0.5,
	Vector3(-1, 0, 0): 0.9,
	Vector3(1, 0, 0): 1.6,
	Vector3(0, -1, 0): 1.9,
}

var env := Environment.new()
var hdr_2d := false


func _ready() -> void:
	var sky_material := ShaderMaterial.new()
	sky_material.shader = Shader.new()
	sky_material.shader.code = "shader_type sky; void sky() { COLOR = vec3(%f); }" % SKY
	env.background_mode = Environment.BG_SKY
	env.sky = Sky.new()
	env.sky.sky_material = sky_material
	env.tonemap_mode = Environment.TONE_MAPPER_LINEAR
	var world_env := WorldEnvironment.new()
	world_env.environment = env
	add_child(world_env)

	var probe := ReflectionProbe.new()  # update mode Once, box projection off
	probe.size = Vector3(20, 20, 20)
	probe.cull_mask = 1  # captures the panels and the sky, not the spheres (layer 2)
	add_child(probe)

	var panel_shader := Shader.new()
	panel_shader.code = "shader_type spatial; render_mode unshaded, cull_disabled; uniform vec3 radiance; void fragment() { ALBEDO = radiance; }"
	for dir: Vector3 in PANELS:
		var quad := QuadMesh.new()
		quad.size = Vector2(8, 8)
		quad.material = ShaderMaterial.new()
		quad.material.shader = panel_shader
		quad.material.set_shader_parameter("radiance", Vector3.ONE * PANELS[dir])
		var panel := MeshInstance3D.new()
		panel.mesh = quad
		add_child(panel)
		panel.look_at_from_position(dir * 9.0, Vector3.ZERO, Vector3.FORWARD if absf(dir.y) > 0.9 else Vector3.UP)

	var mirror := StandardMaterial3D.new()
	mirror.metallic = 1.0
	mirror.roughness = 0.0
	_sphere(mirror, Vector3.ZERO)  # inside the probe
	_sphere(mirror, Vector3(200, 0, 0))  # outside any probe: reflects the sky radiance map
	var coat := StandardMaterial3D.new()  # only the clearcoat lobe reflects anything
	coat.albedo_color = Color.BLACK
	coat.metallic_specular = 0.0
	coat.roughness = 1.0
	coat.clearcoat_enabled = true
	coat.clearcoat = 1.0
	coat.clearcoat_roughness = 0.0
	_sphere(coat, Vector3(-200, 0, 0))  # outside any probe

	var cam := Camera3D.new()  # keeps the scenario (and the probe) rendering during warm-up
	add_child(cam)
	cam.look_at_from_position(Vector3(0, 4, -16), Vector3.ZERO)

	print("%s, %s, %s" % [Engine.get_version_info().string, RenderingServer.get_current_rendering_method(), RenderingServer.get_video_adapter_name()])
	for i in 30:  # let the probe and the sky radiance map finish updating
		await RenderingServer.frame_post_draw
	for hdr in [false, true]:
		hdr_2d = hdr
		await _measure()
	get_tree().quit()


func _measure() -> void:
	print("-- SubViewport.use_hdr_2d = %s" % hdr_2d)
	env.tonemap_exposure = 0.25  # keeps radiance up to 4.0 below 1.0 in the capture
	var targets := PANELS.duplicate()
	targets[Vector3.UP] = SKY
	for dir: Vector3 in targets:
		# Looking out along `dir` sees the panel (or sky) directly; looking back at the mirror sphere,
		# its centre pixel reflects that same panel through the probe.
		var direct := await _radiance(dir * 5.0, dir * 6.0)
		var mirrored := await _radiance(dir * 5.0, Vector3.ZERO)
		print("probe, %-5s radiance %.2f: direct %.3f, mirror in probe %.3f, ratio %.2f" % [
				"sky" if dir == Vector3.UP else "panel", targets[dir], direct, mirrored, mirrored / direct])
	var o := Vector3(200, 0, 0)
	var sky_direct := await _radiance(o + Vector3(0, 0, -5), o + Vector3(0, 0, -10))
	var sky_mirrored := await _radiance(o + Vector3(0, 0, -5), o)
	print("no probe, sky radiance %.2f: direct %.3f, mirror %.3f, ratio %.2f" % [SKY, sky_direct, sky_mirrored, sky_mirrored / sky_direct])
	env.tonemap_exposure = 16.0
	var c := Vector3(-200, 0, 0)
	var coat := await _radiance(c + Vector3(0, 0, -5), c)
	print("no probe, clearcoat sphere centre: %.4f (expected 0.04 * %.2f = %.4f)" % [coat, SKY, 0.04 * SKY])


## Renders the view from `from` to `at` and returns the linear radiance at the centre (5x5 mean / exposure).
func _radiance(from: Vector3, at: Vector3) -> float:
	var vp := SubViewport.new()
	vp.size = Vector2i(256, 256)
	vp.use_hdr_2d = hdr_2d
	vp.render_target_update_mode = SubViewport.UPDATE_ALWAYS
	add_child(vp)
	var cam := Camera3D.new()
	cam.fov = 30.0
	vp.add_child(cam)
	cam.look_at_from_position(from, at, Vector3.FORWARD if absf((at - from).normalized().y) > 0.9 else Vector3.UP)
	for i in 6:
		await RenderingServer.frame_post_draw
	var img := vp.get_texture().get_image()
	vp.queue_free()
	var sum := 0.0
	for y in range(126, 131):
		for x in range(126, 131):
			var px := img.get_pixel(x, y)
			sum += px.g if hdr_2d else px.srgb_to_linear().g  # 8-bit captures are sRGB-encoded
	return sum / 25.0 / env.tonemap_exposure


func _sphere(material: Material, pos: Vector3) -> void:
	var mesh := SphereMesh.new()
	mesh.material = material
	var sphere := MeshInstance3D.new()
	sphere.mesh = mesh
	sphere.layers = 2
	sphere.position = pos
	add_child(sphere)
```

Output on Mobile (4.7.2, HDR 2D off):

```
probe, panel radiance 0.25: direct 0.252, mirror in probe 0.499, ratio 1.98
probe, panel radiance 0.50: direct 0.499, mirror in probe 0.985, ratio 1.97
probe, panel radiance 0.90: direct 0.893, mirror in probe 1.781, ratio 1.99
probe, panel radiance 1.60: direct 1.608, mirror in probe 1.988, ratio 1.24
probe, panel radiance 1.90: direct 1.894, mirror in probe 1.988, ratio 1.05
probe, sky   radiance 0.60: direct 0.600, mirror in probe 1.185, ratio 1.97
no probe, sky radiance 0.60: direct 0.600, mirror 0.588, ratio 0.98
```

The same lines on Forward+ all show `ratio 1.00`.

Related: #124070 (clearcoat sky reflection outside probes on Mobile, a separate cause).
